reasoning: Mandatory answer-first hook test. Direct-claim hooks with a concrete number have been our best reach: 'You're shorter tonight than this morning' reached 108 and 'Why your voice sounds weird' reached 98. So the hook states the fact itself: the brain burns 20% of your energy. Brain energy use is new, well documented, and fits our strongest body and psychology lane. Each slide carries a striking number to hold watch time. The format is a 4-slide reel. Lofi music has been behind 3 of our top 4 reach posts. Palette 4 was used on our two recent near-100 posts. The caption adds a follow reason to target the 0-follow problem, and asks a comparison question.

hook: Your brain burns 20% of your energy

slides.title: Only 2% of your weight
slides.body: An adult brain weighs about 1.4 kg, roughly 2% of your body, yet uses about 20% of your resting energy.
slides.image_prompt: A small glowing brain sculpture on a scale, outweighed by a large stack of stones, warm energy light flowing into the brain

slides.title: Runs on about 20 watts
slides.body: That's roughly the power of a dim light bulb, running nonstop, even while you sleep.
slides.image_prompt: A single dim glowing light bulb in a dark room, its filament shaped like a tiny brain, soft amber glow

slides.title: Hard thinking barely adds
slides.body: A tough problem raises brain energy use only slightly. Most fuel goes to keeping neurons ready to fire.
slides.image_prompt: A dense network of glowing neurons in deep blue, a few brighter sparks among a constantly humming web of light

slides.title: Kids burn even more
slides.body: Around age 5, the brain uses about two-thirds of the body's resting glucose, which may slow body growth.

cta: Follow for a new brain fact daily
caption:
Your brain is only about 2% of your body weight, but at rest it uses about 20% of your energy. That works out to roughly 20 watts, all day and all night.

The twist: thinking hard barely changes that number. Most of the energy goes to keeping billions of neurons ready to fire. In young children it gets even more extreme. Around age 5, the brain takes about two-thirds of the body's resting glucose (Kuzawa et al., PNAS 2014).

Follow for one fact about your body your brain won't believe, every day. Which surprised you more: the 20 watts or the 66%?
